newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH SMES MORE UPBEAT THAN EVER -FEDERATION.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH SMES MORE UPBEAT THAN EVER -FEDERATION.

text.p: Finnish small- and medium-sized companies are more upbeat than ever about their prospects for the next 12 months, the SME lobby, the Federation of Finnish Enterprises, said on Wednesday.
"The cyclical outlook is better than ever before for Finnish SMEs," director Risto Suominen told reporters in connection with the publication of the federation's new business barometer.

In its survey in March, the share of companies seeing improving profitability for the next 12 months rose to 31.6 percent, from 26.1 percent in the previous survey last September, the federation said.
Almost 59 percent of the surveyed firms said they expected profitability to remain unchanged during the next 12 months, while almost 10 percent said profitability would weaken.
The share of companies seeing a better cyclical outlook for their respective sectors over the next 12 months rose to 34.4 percent, from 23.9 percent last autumn, the federation said.
The number of companies with a worse outlook for the next 12 months fell to 6.6 percent in March, from 11.5 percent last autumn, the federation said.
"At the same time, however, while the outlook is better than ever before, companies' plans for expansion are relatively modest -- on a much lower level than in the 1980s," Suominen said.

Just 16.6 percent of the surveyed firms said they planned to expand operations during the next 12 months, while 80.3 percent said they had no plans to expand and 3.1 percent said they would trim back their operations, the federation said.
The sample comprised 1,340 companies, each one with fewer than 200 workers, it said.

During the next 12 months, 17 percent of the firms surveyed said they planned to hire more workers, while 76 percent said their workforces would remain unchanged and almost seven percent said they would reduce staff, the federation said.
Almost 15 percent of the firms said they planned to boost investment in the next 12 months, while 73 percent said investment would be stable, and almost 13 percent said they would invest less.

Altogether 17 percent of the surveyed companies said they expected costs to increase during the next 12 months, whereas more than 74 percent expected costs to remain stable, and 8.6 percent said they saw costs falling, it said.
The hindrances to business development most frequently identified by the SMEs were "unhealthy competition" and high indirect labour costs, the federation said.
